decidedBy: the project owner, 2026-10-29 (RUL-0201), written onto the records by claude-opus-5-5 on 2026-10-29
policy: Where one person may be another, both pages say so, so that a reader on either page sees that the text does not tell whether they are namesakes or one man. Nathanael's page says a tradition identifies him with Bartholomew, and Pharaoh's daughter's that a tradition identifies her with Bithiah; Bartholomew's and Bithiah's pages say the same of them.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's rule of 2026-10-29 that a possible identity is stated on every person it may join

says.notes: He may also be Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, whom Philip brought to Jesus (JHN 1:45-49; 21:2), as a tradition identifies him: Matthew, Mark and Luke name Bartholomew beside Philip, and John never names Bartholomew; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Philip, and Bartholomew' (MAT 10:3): Bartholomew of the twelve, whom Nathanael's page names as the man a tradition identifies him with.

says.notes: She may also be the daughter of Pharaoh who drew Moses out of the water and took him for her son (EXO 2:5-10), as a later tradition identifies her; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, which Mered took' (1CH 4:18): the woman Pharaoh's daughter's page names as the one a later tradition identifies her with.
